title: The Pearl Bet
story: A jar has {w} white, {b} black and {o} gold pearls. You draw 2. You win 3 coins per black pearl and lose 1 per white one; gold pays nothing.
hints: List the possible pairs (WW, WB, BB, WO, BO, OO), the winnings for each, and their probabilities.
Shortcut: by linearity, E = 2 × (expected value of a single draw).
solution: +2 only from one white + one black.
pattern: build the PMF from the cases; or use linearity

title: The Higher Bone
story: Roll a die twice; X is the larger value.
hints: P(X ≤ m) = (m/6)². So what is P(X = m)?

title: The Caravan Insurance
story: You insure a caravan: you pay {A} if it is raided this year, which happens with probability {p}.

phases.ask: What premium gives an expected profit of 10% of A?

hints: E[profit] = premium − A·p.

title: Faulty Arrows
story: A quiver has {N} arrows; {D} are warped. You grab {n}.

phases.ask: Expected number of warped arrows grabbed?

hints: Indicator for each grabbed arrow: P(warped) = ?

title: The Moment Scale
story: A random weight X has E[X] = {m} and Var(X) = {s2}.
hints: E[X²] = Var(X) + (E[X])².
Var(a + bX) = b²Var(X).

title: Pooled Potions Test
story: {N} soldiers are tested for a fever in groups of {g}: one pooled test per group, and if it's positive, everyone in that group is retested individually. Each soldier has the fever independently with probability {p}.
hints: One group: always 1 test, plus g more if anyone is sick. P(someone sick) = ?
solution: Per group: 1 + g(1 − (1−p)^g). Multiply by N/g groups.
pattern: expected cost via a per-unit indicator

title: The Blindfold Exam
story: An exam has {n} riddles with {c} options each. You guess blindly.
hints: Number correct ~ Binomial(n, 1/c).
solution: Binomial tail from k to n.

title: The Seer's Claim
story: A seer claims second sight. A fair coin is flipped {n} times and she gets {k} or more right.

phases.ask: P(at least {k} right by pure luck)?

hints: If she has no gift, her number correct is Binomial(n, 1/2).

title: Reverse Engineering
story: A binomial count has mean 8 and variance 4.8.
hints: np = 8 and np(1−p) = 4.8. Divide the second by the first.
pattern: solve for (n, p) from the moments

title: The Council of Judges
story: {n} judges each reach the right verdict independently with probability {p}. The majority decides.
hints: The majority is right when at least (n+1)/2 judges are right.

title: The Scribe's Errors
story: The royal scribe averages {l} errors per page.

phases.ask: P(a page has 2 or more errors)?

hints: Rare events across many opportunities → which distribution?

title: The Lottery of 400
story: {n} independent lottery tickets each win with probability {p}.
hints: λ = np.
solution: Poisson(np) is a good approximation when n is large and p is small.

title: Gate Arrivals
story: Travellers reach the gate at an average rate of 1 every {r} minutes.
hints: Scale the rate to the window: λ = window/r.
pattern: Poisson with the rate scaled to the time window

title: Waiting for the Six
story: You roll a die until the first six.

phases.ask: P(the first six is on roll {k})?

hints: k−1 failures and then a success.

title: The Third Victory
story: You win each joust with probability {p}. You keep jousting until your {r}rd win.
hints: The last joust must be a win; place the other r−1 wins among the first n−1 jousts.

title: The Inspector's Crates
story: A crate of {N} lanterns has {D} broken ones. The inspector tests {n} at random and accepts the crate only if all {n} work.
hints: Sampling without replacement → hypergeometric with 0 broken.

title: The Red-Bet System
story: A 'sure-win' system: bet 1 on red (P = 18/38). If you win, stop. If you lose, bet 1 on red twice more, then stop.
hints: List the outcomes: W; LWW; LWL/LLW; LLL. What is the net result of each?
Is P(ahead) > ½ while E < 0 a contradiction?
solution: E ≈ −0.108: you win small often and lose big rarely.

title: The Staircase Scroll
hints: Jump sizes are the PMF.
P(a < X ≤ b) = F(b) − F(a).
pattern: read the PMF off the CDF jumps

title: First to Two
story: Two knights duel until one has 2 wins. You win each bout with probability {p}.
hints: The match lasts 2 bouts if the first two have the same winner; otherwise 3.

title: Who Pays for Mead?
story: Three friends flip coins; the 'odd one out' pays. If all three match, they flip again.
hints: P(all match) = 2/8. Rounds until the first 'odd one out' is geometric.

title: The Spice Speculator
story: You hold 1000 coins. Spice costs 2 coins an ounce today; next week it will cost 1 or 4, each with probability 1/2.

phases.ask: Buy everything now: expected value of your spice next week, in coins?
To maximise the expected OUNCES you hold, wait a week then buy: expected ounces?
Which goal do you pursue if you plan to sell next week? (choose)

hints: Expected value is linear in what you are measuring. Measure coins in one case and ounces in the other.
solution: If you'll sell for coins, maximise coins: buy now.
pattern: which quantity are you taking the expectation of?
